mainTopic: Twilight views, the laws of כתמים (stains), and the משנה on blood seen at בין השמשות on borderline days
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer: two ברייתות disagree about whether the בין השמשות of רבי יוסי comes after the בין השמשות of רבי יהודה or falls inside its end. Next comes a ברייתא about a כתם. רבי says it makes the woman and קדשים impure retroactively. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that a stain should never be stricter than actually seeing blood, and the גמרא rewords his view so that this holds even for קדשים. A second ברייתא asks when a stain can be connected to a later sighting of blood: within 24 hours according to רבי, or only on the same day according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. רבי's comment that the other view 'fixes' her situation is explained two ways. רבינא reverses it, and רב נחמן says it refers to the laws of זיבה. Then רבי זירא learns from רבי אסי that כתמים need a הפסק טהרה. Finally, a new משנה discusses a woman who sees blood at בין השמשות on borderline days. רב חסדא explains its labels, and the גמרא begins asking about רבי יהושע's comment on the 'misguided' women, a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two views on how the two twilights fit together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining that the two ברייתות disagree about whether the בין השמשות of רבי יוסי comes after the בין השמשות of רבי יהודה or falls inside its end.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and only after that does the twilight of רבי יוסי begin. But this other תנא holds that the twilight of רבי יוסי stretches into, and is part of, the twilight of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to a contradiction between two ברייתות. It explains that each ברייתא follows a different view of how the two definitions of twilight line up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first תנא, the בין השמשות of רבי יוסי starts only after the בין השמשות of רבי יהודה is over. So checking during רבי יהודה's twilight does not cover רבי יוסי's. According to the second תנא, רבי יוסי's twilight falls inside the end of רבי יהודה's. So a woman who checked through all of רבי יהודה's twilight has also covered רבי יוסי's.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight, the doubtful time between day and night
Takes effect, begins
Stretches into and is part of
A teacher of the ברייתא or משנה period

steps.confusionAlert: There are not two separate twilights every evening. These are two different opinions about when twilight happens. This step is about how those two opinions overlap in time.

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר חָיֵיל בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: and afterward the twilight of Rabbi Yosei begins,
but this tanna holds,
the twilight of Rabbi Yosei
stretches into and belongs within that of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a resolution that began on the earlier part of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each ברייתא follows a different view on how the two twilights overlap.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to contradict each other about a woman who checked during twilight.
steps.terutzMaskana: No real contradiction: one תנא puts רבי יוסי's twilight after רבי יהודה's, and the other puts it inside the end of רבי יהודה's.

steps.title: רבי: a stain makes her and קדשים impure retroactively
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that according to רבי, a woman who finds a כתם makes both herself and קדשים impure retroactively.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A woman who sees a blood stain makes herself and holy items impure going backward in time. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in which רבי rules that a כתם makes things impure retroactively, both for the woman herself and for קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we do not know when the stain got onto the garment, we treat her as impure going back to the time the garment was last washed. According to רבי, this applies fully. She counts as impure for everything she touched in that period, and so do the קדשים she touched.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on a garment or body, without feeling a flow
Retroactively, going backward in time
Holy items, such as sacrifices and sanctified food
She counts herself as impure, so things she touched become impure

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A woman who sees a stain —
renders herself and consecrated items impure retroactively,
phrases.notes: Going back to the time that garment was last washed.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about stains.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, a כתם makes both the woman and קדשים impure retroactively.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: only קדשים, not herself
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that the כתם makes קדשים impure retroactively but not the woman herself, so that her stain is not stricter than actually seeing blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: She makes holy items impure, but she does not make herself impure, so that her stain should not be stricter than her actually seeing blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The second opinion in the ברייתא disagrees with רבי. He limits the retroactive impurity to קדשים only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is a comparison. When a woman actually sees blood, she makes things impure only going back about 24 hours, not back to when her garment was washed. A stain, which is weaker than actually seeing blood, should not reach back further. So for her own impurity, the כתם does not go back to the washing.

keyTerms.meaning: Stricter, more severe
Her actual seeing of blood, an actual flow
So that it should not be

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
consecrated items — she renders impure,
herself — she does not render impure,
so that her stain should not be more stringent than her seeing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי's ruling in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כתם makes קדשים impure retroactively but not the woman herself, because a stain should not be stricter than seeing blood.
steps.whyThisMatters: His principle that a stain should not be stricter than seeing blood is exactly what the גמרא is about to test.

steps.title: But for קדשים the stain is stricter than seeing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: in his own ruling, for קדשים the stain is stricter than actually seeing blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we find that her stain is stricter than her seeing when it comes to holy items!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's reasoning using his own words. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He said a stain should not be stricter than seeing. Yet he rules that for קדשים, a stain reaches back to the washing of the garment, which is further back than seeing blood would reach. So his own principle seems broken in the case of קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, introducing a challenge
We find
With regard to

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not challenging רבי here. It is pointing out a tension inside רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's own ruling.

phrases.english: But don't we find,
her stain more stringent than her seeing
with regard to consecrated items!
phrases.notes: That is his own ruling from the previous line: the stain makes קדשים impure all the way back to the washing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gave in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's principle that a stain should not be stricter than seeing blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own ruling on קדשים makes the stain reach further back than seeing blood would, so the stain is stricter there. That contradicts his stated reason.

steps.title: Rewording רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: a stain is never stricter than seeing
steps.stepSummary: To answer the challenge, the גמרא changes the wording of the ברייתא. Now רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says the כתם does not make even קדשים impure further back in time, so the stain is never stricter than ראיה in any matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, teach the ברייתא this way: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says she does not make even קדשים impure going backward, so that her stain should not be stricter than her actually seeing blood, in any matter at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 4 by correcting how the ברייתא should be read. In the new reading, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is lenient for קדשים too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4 the problem was that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר made the stain stricter than ראיה for קדשים. The new reading removes that problem: a stain does not make קדשים impure further back than a real sighting would. Now his reason fits his whole ruling, with no exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach it like this, meaning read the ברייתא with this corrected wording
Consecrated items, like sacrificial food
Actually seeing a flow of blood
More stringent, stricter

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר (in the corrected reading), a כתם is never stricter than ראיה, not even for קדשים.

phrases.english: Rather, teach it like this:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
even consecrated items she does not make impure,
phrases.notes: He means she doesn't make them impure going back in time, further than a real sighting would.

phrases.english: so that her stain should not be more stringent
than her seeing of blood, in any matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 4 by changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר made קדשים impure going back in time, which made the stain stricter than seeing blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר does not make even קדשים impure going back in time, so the stain is never stricter than seeing blood.

steps.title: רבי: a stain followed by blood within 24 hours is joined to the sighting
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: a woman found a stain and later saw blood. רבי rules that if the blood came within 24 hours, she treats the stain as part of that sighting.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if she saw a stain and afterward saw blood, she connects her stain to her sighting, as long as it was within 24 hours. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a stain that is followed by a real flow of blood. This step gives רבי's view, and the next step gives the other opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Connecting the stain to the sighting is a leniency. The stain is treated as the start of this flow, so she is impure only from when she found it, and not further back in time. רבי allows this whenever the blood comes within a full 24-hour period.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on a garment or body, not felt as a flow
She connects or attributes (the stain to the sighting)
A full 24-hour period, from one time of day to the same time the next day

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If she saw a stain,
and afterward she saw blood —
she attributes her stain to her seeing of blood
within twenty-four hours; these are the words of Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: רָאֲתָה כֶּתֶם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ רָאֲתָה דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: what happens when a stain is followed by a real flow of blood
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, a stain followed by blood within 24 hours is connected to that sighting.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: only if the blood comes that same day
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says she may connect the stain to the sighting only if the blood came on the same day she found the stain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: only on that same day.
steps.whatsHappening: The second opinion in the ברייתא disagrees with רבי about how long she has to see blood for the stain to be connected to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A calendar day can be shorter than 24 hours. If she found the stain late in the day, the next day may still be within 24 hours. In that case רבי connects the stain to the sighting, but רבי שמעון בן אלעזר does not. So רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is the stricter opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Its day, meaning the same day the stain was found

steps.confusionAlert: 'Same day' is NOT more generous than '24 hours'. A day can end only a few hours after she found the stain. That is why רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is the stricter one here.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
On that day.
phrases.notes: Only if the blood comes on the same day she found the stain can she connect them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: יוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, she connects the stain to the sighting only if the blood came on the same day she found the stain.

steps.title: רבי praises the other view for 'fixing' her situation
steps.stepSummary: רבי says that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view seems better than his own, because it makes things easier for the woman while his own view makes things harder for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: his words seem better than mine, because he fixes her situation and I ruin it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי comments on the dispute and says the other opinion looks more correct, because it is easier on the woman. This sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that for stains we should prefer the view that helps the woman. But רבי is calling רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view the easier one, even though in Step 7 it turned out to be the stricter one. That mismatch is what the גמרא will attack next.

keyTerms.meaning: His words seem more correct
Fixes her situation, meaning he rules leniently for her
Ruins her situation, meaning he rules strictly against her

phrases.english: Rabbi said: His words appear more correct than my words,
for he fixes her situation,
and I ruin her situation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי gives his opinion on the dispute just presented
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי prefers the view that is easier on the woman, which he says is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view.

steps.title: But רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is actually the stricter one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: how can רבי שמעון בן אלעזר be called the one who 'fixes' her situation, when his view is actually the stricter one?
steps.simpleTranslation: He fixes her situation? He ruins her situation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי's praise, because it does not match the two rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי, blood that comes the next day but within 24 hours still lets her connect the stain to the sighting, which is a leniency. Under רבי שמעון בן אלעזר it does not, so she is impure further back in time. That means רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is the one who makes things harder for her.

keyTerms.meaning: He truly ruins her situation, meaning his ruling is the strict one

phrases.english: He fixes her situation?
He ruins her situation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's statement in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's claim that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view is the easier one for the woman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A same-day limit is narrower than a 24-hour limit, so רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view is the stricter one, not the easier one.

steps.title: רבינא: reverse the praise
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that רבי's statement must be reversed. The correct reading is: my words seem better than his, because I fix her situation and he ruins it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא solves the problem by saying that רבי's comment should be read the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the comment is reversed, רבי praises his own lenient view, which is the 24-hour limit. Now the reason fits the rulings: for stains, follow the view that is easier on the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it, meaning switch the wording around

steps.whatToRemember: After רבינא's correction, רבי's 24-hour view is the lenient one, and רבי himself says it is the better view because it is easier on the woman.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Reverse it.
phrases.notes: Switch רבי's comment around so that he says his own view fixes her situation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9 by reversing רבי's statement
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי praised רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view as the easier one.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי praises his own 24-hour view as the easier one for the woman, and calls רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view the stricter one.

steps.title: רב נחמן keeps רבי's original wording
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says we do not need to reverse רבי's statement. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view really does help her when it comes to the laws of זיבה, and רבי's own view makes things harder for her there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Actually, do not reverse it. He (רבי שמעון בן אלעזר) fixes her laws with regard to זיבה, and I ruin her laws with regard to זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a different answer to the question from step 9. He keeps רבי's words exactly as they were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר does not connect the stain to blood seen the next day, so her count of days starts from the actual sighting. Blood she sees eight days after the stain can then still fall inside her נדה days, and she is not a זבה קטנה. Under רבי's view the count starts from the stain, so that same blood counts as זיבה. On this question, רבי's view is the stricter one.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really. It signals that we keep the original reading.
Do not reverse it, meaning do not switch the wording.
Bleeding outside the normal נדה days, which can make her a זבה
A woman who sees זיבה blood for one or two days and must then keep a clean day

steps.confusionAlert: Both answers are about the same statement. רבינא flips the words. רב נחמן keeps the words but says 'fixes' and 'ruins' refer to זיבה. Seen that way, the 'stricter' view in one area becomes the easier view in another.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one view can be easier on one point and harder on another. Here the stain view affects how her days of נדה and זיבה are counted.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman says:
Actually, do not reverse it,
phrases.notes: He is disagreeing with רבינא from step 10, who flipped רבי's words.

phrases.english: for he fixes her laws with regard to זיבה,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. רבי is still the one speaking.

phrases.english: and I ruin her laws with regard to זיבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם לָא תֵּיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the קשיא of step 9 and rejects the need for רבינא's reversal in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the area of law: the 'fixing' refers to זיבה, not to stains themselves
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is simply stricter, so he cannot be called the one who 'fixes' her situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the laws of זיבה, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view is easier, so רבי's original words stand.

steps.title: Do stains require a הפסק טהרה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רבי אסי whether a woman who is טמאה because of a stain must do a הפסק טהרה check, just like a woman who actually saw blood. רבי אסי does not answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked רבי אסי: Do stains require a הפסק טהרה or not? He was silent and did not say anything to him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי זירא asks a practical question about stains, and his teacher stays silent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who sees blood must check that the bleeding has stopped, a הפסק טהרה, before she starts becoming טהורה. The question is whether a stain, which is a lesser kind of טומאה, needs this step too. רבי אסי is silent for now; he answers in Step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Stains of blood found on her body or clothing
A check showing the bleeding has stopped, the first step toward becoming טהורה
He was silent

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked Rabbi Asi:

phrases.aramaic: כְּתָמִים צְרִיכִין הֶפְסֵק טׇהֳרָה אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: Do stains require a stopping-check for purity, or not?

phrases.aramaic: אִשְׁתִּיק, וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵי.
phrases.english: He was silent, and did not say anything at all to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about stains after the discussion of רבי's statement is finished.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a woman who is טמאה only because of a stain needs a הפסק טהרה like a woman who saw blood

steps.title: רבי אסי is later found teaching רבי's rule
steps.stepSummary: On another occasion, רבי זירא finds רבי אסי sitting and teaching: a woman connects her stain to her sighting within twenty-four hours, which is the view of רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time he found him sitting and saying: She connects her stain to her sighting within twenty-four hours. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that later רבי זירא heard רבי אסי teach רבי's rule about stains. This sets up the next move, which links back to the question that went unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same rule of רבי we saw in step 6. Hearing his teacher say it gives רבי זירא an opening to come back to his question about הפסק טהרה for stains.

keyTerms.meaning: Another time, on a different occasion
She connects or attributes, here linking the stain to the sighting
A full twenty-four-hour period

phrases.english: Another time he found him sitting and saying:
phrases.notes: רבי זירא is the one who found רבי אסי teaching.

phrases.english: She connects her stain to her sighting
within twenty-four hours; these are the words of רבי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רבי זירא and רבי אסי, preparing a link between רבי's stain rule and the unanswered question of step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman connects her stain to blood she sees within twenty-four hours (רבי).

steps.title: ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue about whether she must have checked
steps.stepSummary: Continuing רבי אסי's teaching, ריש לקיש says the כתם connects to the sighting only if she did a בדיקה. רבי יוחנן says it connects even if she did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: This is only where she checked herself. And רבי יוחנן said: Even if she did not check herself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי is still teaching the rule from Step 13, that a woman connects her כתם to her sighting within twenty-four hours. Now he adds a dispute about the details of that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש limits the rule: the connection works only if she did a בדיקה. רבי יוחנן disagrees and says the connection works even without a בדיקה. This sets up רבי זירא's inference in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Only if; this phrase adds a condition to a rule
She checked herself (did a בדיקה)
Even though not; the rule applies anyway

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: This is only where she checked herself,
phrases.notes: "This" means the rule from Step 13, that she connects her stain to her sighting within twenty-four hours.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא בָּדְקָה.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan said: even if she did not check herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a dispute about the details of רבי אסי's teaching from Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to ריש לקיש, a כתם connects to her sighting only if she did a בדיקה. According to רבי יוחנן, it connects even without a בדיקה.

steps.title: רבי זירא infers that stains need a הפסק טהרה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רבי אסי: does this dispute show that כתמים need a הפסק טהרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: Does this mean, by implication, that stains require a הפסק טהרה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא hears the dispute and draws a conclusion from it. This is the very question he asked earlier in Step 12 without getting an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides of the dispute talk about whether she checked herself. To רבי זירא, that suggests a woman with a כתם needs a check to end her טומאה, just like a woman who saw blood. He asks רבי אסי to confirm this.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies that; the speaker is drawing an inference
Stains of blood found on a woman's body or clothing
A check showing that her bleeding has stopped, which begins her return to טהרה

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי זירא is speaking to רבי אסי.

phrases.english: Does this imply that stains require
a הפסק טהרה?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean the same thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the dispute in Step 14 that answers רבי זירא's unanswered question from Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dispute implies that a woman who is טמאה from a כתם needs a הפסק טהרה.

steps.title: רבי אסי confirms: yes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי agrees that כתמים do need a הפסק טהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers רבי זירא's inference with one word: yes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the question from Step 12 that רבי אסי had left unanswered. A woman who is טמאה because of a כתם needs a הפסק טהרה, just like a woman who actually saw blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes (Aramaic)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אסי, a woman who is טמאה because of a כתם also needs a הפסק טהרה.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the inference question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, כתמים require a הפסק טהרה.

steps.title: Why didn't you answer me all those other times?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא points out that he asked many times and got no answer, and asks whether the answer came to רבי אסי during his learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But many times I asked you, and you did not say anything. Perhaps it came to you in the flow of your learning?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא is surprised. He asked this question many times and got silence, so he asks whether the answer only now came back to רבי אסי while he was teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the ruling itself. רבי זירא wants to understand why רבי אסי was silent before, and he suggests the answer came out naturally as רבי אסי reviewed his material.

keyTerms.meaning: Many times
Nothing at all
In the flow of your learning; while you were going through your studies

phrases.english: But many times
I asked you,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording, meaning "I asked."

phrases.english: and you did not say anything at all,
perhaps it came to you in the flow of your learning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts רבי אסי's answer in Step 16 with his silence in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אסי only now remembered the answer while going through his learning.

steps.title: רבי אסי admits it came to him while learning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי confirms that the answer came to him in the flow of his learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, it came to me in the flow of my learning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי agrees with רבי זירא's guess. The answer came back to him as he was going through his studies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the silence in Step 12. רבי אסי could not give the answer when he was asked directly, but it came out once he was reviewing the topic in order.

keyTerms.meaning: My flow of learning

steps.whatToRemember: The story ends with רבי אסי confirming that כתמים need a הפסק טהרה. He had remembered this only while reviewing his learning.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
in the flow of my learning it came to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question from Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the answer came to him while going through his learning.

steps.title: New משנה: seeing blood at twilight on the eleventh day
steps.stepSummary: A woman who sees blood at בין השמשות on the eleventh day is treated with both possibilities: as the start and end of נדה, and as the start and end of זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A woman who sees blood on the eleventh day at twilight is treated as the beginning of נדה and the end of נדה, the beginning of זיבה and the end of זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins here. It deals with a woman who sees blood at בין השמשות on the eleventh day of the days of זיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בין השמשות might belong to the day that is ending or to the night that is starting. The day might be the eleventh day, which is part of זיבה, or the next day, which starts נדה. So she is treated in both ways at once: as if starting and ending נדה, and as if starting and ending זיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (shortened in the text as מַתְנִי')
Twilight; the uncertain time between day and night
A woman in the seven days of her regular period
Bleeding outside the regular period, during the eleven days between periods
The eleventh day, the last of the days of זיבה

steps.confusionAlert: "Beginning of נדה and end of נדה" does not mean two separate events. It means that because of the doubt, she is treated with both possibilities at the same time.

phrases.english: Mishnah: One who sees blood on the eleventh day
phrases.notes: This means the eleventh of the days of זיבה, which come between her periods.

phrases.english: at twilight —
is treated as the beginning of נדה and the end of נדה,
the beginning of זיבה and the end of זיבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָרוֹאָה יוֹם אַחַד עָשָׂר בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the end of the רבי זירא and רבי אסי story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood seen at בין השמשות on the eleventh day is treated with all the possibilities: the beginning and end of נדה, and the beginning and end of זיבה.

steps.title: Twilight after childbirth, and the women are called טועות
steps.stepSummary: The same doubt applies at בין השמשות on the fortieth day after a boy or the eightieth day after a girl. All these women are called טועות.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the fortieth day for a male and the eightieth day for a female, at twilight in all of these cases, these women are mistaken.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds more twilight cases from the days after giving birth. It then gives all of these women the label טועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fortieth day after a boy and the eightieth day after a girl are the last days of the special period after birth. Blood seen at בין השמשות on those days might belong to the last day or to the next day. Because of this doubt, these women, like the woman in Step 19, are called טועות: their count of days has become uncertain.

keyTerms.meaning: The fortieth day after giving birth to a boy
The eightieth day after giving birth to a girl
Mistaken women; women who are unsure about their count of days

steps.whatToRemember: Whenever blood is seen at בין השמשות on a borderline day, the woman's count becomes uncertain, and the משנה calls her a טועה.

phrases.english: The fortieth day for a male,
phrases.notes: He means forty days after giving birth to a boy.

phrases.english: and the eightieth day for a female,
at twilight in all of them —
these are mistaken women.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם אַרְבָּעִים לַזָּכָר, וְיוֹם שְׁמוֹנִים לַנְּקֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the childbirth cases to the twilight case of Step 19 and gives all of them one label.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women who see blood at בין השמשות on the eleventh day, or on the fortieth or eightieth day after birth, are טועות.

steps.title: Help the clever women, not only the confused ones
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע tells the חכמים: instead of making rules for the confused women, come make rules for the clever women.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: While you are busy fixing things for the foolish women, come and fix things for the clever women.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. רבי יהושע pushes the discussion away from the confused women (the טועות) and toward women who do know their dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rules dealt with women who lost track of their days. רבי יהושע says the more useful job is guiding women who know exactly when they saw blood. They still need help because they saw many times and the counting gets complicated.

keyTerms.meaning: Foolish women; here, women who mixed up or forgot their days
Clever, competent women who know when they saw blood
To fix, to make rules or provisions for

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
While you are fixing things for the foolish women,
phrases.notes: He means the טועות from the step before, the women who lost track of their days.

phrases.english: come and fix things for the clever women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the cases of the טועות listed in steps 19-20
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rules should also be made for the competent women who know their dates but have complicated sightings.

steps.title: The משנה's wording does not fit the case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: how can the eleventh-day case be called 'beginning of נדה and end of נדה'? The real doubt is 'beginning of נדה or end of זיבה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'Beginning of נדה and end of נדה'? It is really 'beginning of נדה and end of זיבה!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and goes straight back to the משנה's ruling from step 19. It challenges the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the seven days of נדה come eleven days of זיבה. Blood at בין השמשות of the eleventh day might belong to the day, which makes it the end of זיבה. Or it might belong to the night, which makes it the start of a new נדה. So 'end of נדה' makes no sense here.

keyTerms.meaning: The start of a new נדה period
The last of the eleven זיבה days

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not arguing with the law of the משנה. It is only asking why the משנה describes the eleventh-day doubt with the label 'end of נדה.'

phrases.english: Gemara
Beginning of נדה and end of נדה?
phrases.notes: This is quoting the משנה's ruling about the eleventh day, from step 19.

phrases.english: It is beginning of נדה and end of זיבה!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּחִלַּת נִדָּה וְסוֹף נִדָּה? תְּחִלַּת נִדָּה וְסוֹף זִיבָה הִיא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי יהושע's comment and goes back to the משנה's ruling in step 19 to question its wording
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's phrase 'beginning of נדה and end of נדה' for the eleventh day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The eleventh day is the last day of זיבה, so the doubt can only be new נדה versus end of זיבה, never end of נדה.

steps.title: רב חסדא rereads the eleventh-day case
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the משנה means: blood at בין השמשות on the eleventh day is a doubt between the beginning of נדה and the end of זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This is what the משנה means. A woman who sees blood on the eleventh day at בין השמשות is in doubt between the beginning of נדה and the end of זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by explaining what the משנה really means. For the eleventh day, he agrees the pair is 'beginning of נדה / end of זיבה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not change the law. He matches each label to the right case. The eleventh-day case gets the labels the גמרא said it should have. That leaves the משנה's other phrase to be placed somewhere else, which the next step does.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; used to reread a source
Twilight, when it is unclear whether it is still day or already night
The eleventh day, the last of the זיבה days

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
This is what it is saying:
One who sees blood on the eleventh day
at twilight,
it is beginning of נדה and end of זיבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading of the משנה, matching each label to the correct case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to call the eleventh-day doubt 'beginning of נדה and end of נדה.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The eleventh-day doubt is beginning of נדה versus end of זיבה.

steps.title: The seventh day of נדה: end of נדה or beginning of זיבה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא continues: blood at בין השמשות on the seventh day of נדה is a doubt between the end of נדה and the beginning of זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on the seventh day of her נדה, it is the end of נדה and the beginning of זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא finishes his rereading. He explains the משנה's other phrase as a second case: blood at twilight on the seventh day of נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If that twilight still counts as day, the blood is the end of נדה. If it counts as night, it is the start of the זיבה days. So the labels 'end of נדה' and 'beginning of זיבה' belong to this case, and every label in the משנה now has a proper place.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh, last day of her נדה period
The last day of the נדה period
The first of the eleven זיבה days

steps.whatToRemember: Twilight on day 11 of זיבה means a doubt between the start of נדה and the end of זיבה. Twilight on day 7 of נדה means a doubt between the end of נדה and the start of זיבה. Either way, she is treated strictly for both possibilities.

phrases.english: And on the seventh day of her נדה —
it is end of נדה and beginning of זיבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חסדא's rereading by placing the משנה's other phrase in the seventh-day case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading that splits the משנה's labels into two separate twilight cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's labels seemed mismatched with its cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: The seventh day of נדה at twilight is a doubt of end of נדה versus beginning of זיבה.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהושע and starting to question the word 'misguided'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע's line from the משנה about the שוטות and begins a question about these women with the word הני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: Instead of fixing things for the misguided women, and so on. These women...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע's words from the משנה so it can talk about them. Then it starts a question with 'these women...'. This line is setting up a question that is finished in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהושע called the women who saw blood at בין השמשות 'שוטות', meaning misguided. Back in Step 20, though, these same women were called טועות, women who are confused or mistaken. With the word הני, the גמרא starts asking about these very women, so its focus is on the word שוטות.

keyTerms.meaning: Misguided or foolish women. This is רבי יהושע's word for the women in doubt.
Fixing, or making rules and provisions for someone.
Literally 'while you are...'. Here it means 'instead of'.
These (Aramaic). The גמרא uses it to point to the women just mentioned.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this is a brand-new statement. The גמרא is repeating the משנה's words on purpose so it can now ask about them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the line from the משנה we saw back in Step 21.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁאַתֶּם מְתַקְּנִין אֶת הַשּׁוֹטוֹת כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Instead of you fixing things for the misguided women, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means the rest of the line is assumed: come fix things for the clever women.

phrases.english: These women...

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: עַד שֶׁאַתֶּם מְתַקְּנִין אֶת הַשּׁוֹטוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing רב חסדא's explanation of the eleventh-day and seventh-day cases, the גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה, רבי יהושע's remark.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's word שוטות (misguided) for the women who saw blood at בין השמשות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גמרא begins asking about 'these' women, the ones רבי יהושע called שוטות. The full question is finished in the next part of the text.
